value.text: For any group of customers who each buy the same number of DVDs, the group's total is the group size times the number each customer buys.
Billy's Tuesday customers are exactly these three groups and no others: the first 3, the next 2 and the last 3 (3 + 2 + 3 = 8).
Billy sold 3 DVDs to his first 3 customers.
value.cot_quote: Total DVDs sold to these customers = \(3 \times 1 = 3\).

value.text: Billy sold 0 DVDs to his last 3 customers.

value.text: Apply the group-total rule to the first 3 customers, who buy 1 DVD each.
value.cot_quote: Total DVDs sold to these customers = \(3 \times 1 = 3\).

value.text: Apply the group-total rule to the next 2 customers, who buy 2 DVDs each.
value.cot_quote: Total DVDs sold to these customers = \(2 \times 2 = 4\).

value.text: Apply the group-total rule to the last 3 customers, who buy no DVDs.
value.cot_quote: Total DVDs sold to these customers = \(0 \times 3 = 0\).

value.text: Sum the three group totals to get the total DVDs sold, treating the three groups as all 8 customers.
value.cot_quote: Total DVDs sold = \(3 + 4 + 0 = 7\).
